name: Amla
ancientUse: Rasayana for vitality; supports digestion and immunity in Ayurveda.
modernScience: Rich in vitamin C and polyphenols; studied for antioxidant and metabolic support.

name: Tulsi (Holy Basil)
ancientUse: Used to support respiratory health and clarity; considered an adaptogenic herb.
modernScience: Contains eugenol and other compounds; studied for stress response and antimicrobial activity.

name: Ginger (Adrak)
ancientUse: Kindles agni (digestive fire) and helps reduce heaviness after meals.
modernScience: Gingerols may support digestion and help with nausea; researched for anti-inflammatory effects.

name: Ashwagandha
ancientUse: Traditionally used to support strength, recovery, and calm the nervous system.
modernScience: Withanolides studied for stress reduction and sleep quality in some clinical trials.

name: Brahmi (Bacopa)
ancientUse: Used for memory and mental calm; supports medhya (cognitive) balance.
modernScience: Bacosides studied for cognitive support and stress modulation.

name: Triphala
ancientUse: Classic blend for gentle detox support and regular digestion.
modernScience: Polyphenol-rich; studied for gut motility and antioxidant properties.

name: Jeera (Cumin)
ancientUse: Used to aid digestion and reduce gas after heavier meals.
modernScience: Cumin essential oils studied for digestive support and possible glycemic benefits.

name: Saunf (Fennel)
ancientUse: Traditionally chewed after meals to freshen breath and support digestion.
modernScience: Anethole studied for digestive comfort and antispasmodic effects.

name: Cardamom (Elaichi)
ancientUse: Used for aromatic digestion support and to reduce heaviness.
modernScience: Contains cineole and terpenes; researched for antioxidant and digestive benefits.

name: Turmeric (Haldi)
ancientUse: Supports healthy inflammation balance and helps clear ama (metabolic toxins).
modernScience: Curcumin studied for anti-inflammatory and antioxidant activity; absorption improves with fat/pepper.
